title: Four O'Clock Prices
logline: Before dawn at a wholesale vegetable market the lorries all arrive at once, prices move by the minute, and a trader holds buyers, a phone and a scale together until the rush breaks into sudden quiet.
human_question: What happens to our attention when everything arrives at once?

situation.what_happens: Produce comes in overnight from many growing areas and has to be sold before it loses value, so a whole day's trade is compressed into a few hours in the dark. A trader takes delivery, sets and resets prices as supply shifts, weighs, argues, answers a phone and keeps a running account of who owes what, all at the same time. Counts are lost and started again and sentences are left unfinished. Then the last sacks go and the noise stops all at once.
situation.who_is_involved: A trader who carries the stall's risk; the drivers and loaders who set the pace; the buyers, who can always walk to the next stall; and the growers, absent, whose season is settled by the prices agreed here.
situation.what_is_at_stake: Money that is immediate and real: spoilage, a price agreed a minute too late, a debt owed to a grower, the next planting. For a trader's household a single night can decide a month.
situation.how_it_unfolds: It begins in the dark with arrival and ends in daylight on an empty floor. The pressure peaks when supply and buyers coincide, and something is usually nearly missed. It ends in exhaustion, a cup of tea, a count reconciled or left. Reality decides how heavy the night is: how much came in, what the weather did to the crop that week, who turned up to buy.

concept_merge.why_together: C008 gives the mechanism: restlessness is the loss of one-pointedness, the mind's power to stay with a single object, and when that power breaks the mind's other faculties are thrown off with it [C008-P:L62]; the sources tie it to sudden situations, to doing many things at once and to working in a hurry [C008-M:L16–L20]. C074 gives the image and the frame: the compendium counts restlessness among the states that cover the mind, likens it to water ruffled by the wind, and answers it with plain practical helps rather than effort [C074-P:L348–L358]. Together they let a working night show a state rather than a failing.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That scattered attention is made by conditions before it is made by character. C008 alone would put the fault inside the trader; C074 alone would leave the state a category. Together the viewer feels the scattering in their own attention, then the stillness after it, and understands that it is the wind that ruffles the water.

concept_links.why: The digest ties the restless mind to sudden situations, to doing many things at once and to working in a hurry, and explains it as the breaking of the mind's power to stay with one object, which throws the rest of the mind off course [C008-M:L16–L20; C008-P:L62]. The market shows those conditions and nothing about anyone's inner state. The digest's warning is carried in the film's design: restlessness is not a productivity problem with a mindfulness tip for an answer.

The compendium's image for restlessness is a surface of water ruffled by the wind, and it places the state among those that cover the mind and stop it settling [C074-P:L348–L358]. The film can hold the rush and the calm after it without naming anything.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: When everything arrives at once, attention scatters. The texts compare this restlessness to water ruffled by the wind, and name rushing and doing many things at once as the moments when it tends to arise.
what_must_be_real: The trader's work, prices, debts and pressures. Nothing is arranged, slowed or repeated; no rush is manufactured and no quiet is requested.
position_hint: middle: the group's second face of confusion, the mind that cannot stay, set against the mind that cannot settle. It also earns the closing turn by giving the viewer something to slow down from.
risks: Making busy working people look like an illustration of a mental flaw.
Chaos footage with no person at its centre.
Reading the quiet afterwards as equanimity; the digest says the flat neutrality of these states is not peace.
Safety in a crowded working space.
drop_if: No trader will let the camera stay with them through the whole rush.

connections.note: The rush that scatters attention here is answered at the close of the group by work that can only be done slowly.
A public, commercial rush against a private, devotional one.

selection.reason: Carries the group's third episode and is the only idea that shows restlessness as something conditions produce.

unknowns: No participant or event has been found or confirmed. Everything here is a research direction.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. No location, scene or shot decisions are made at the idea stage.
